title: Modified ZN Staining Protocol
author: Asar Khan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tb2eiqe

steps.title: Prepare Stool Smear
steps.instruction: Spread the stool sample evenly on the middle of the slide using constant rotational movement for 5 to 10 minutes.

steps.title: Air-Dry Slides
steps.instruction: Place slides on a dryer with the smeared surface facing upwards to air-dry for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Fix Smear
steps.instruction: Fix the dried smear using absolute methanol for 3-5 minutes.

steps.title: Apply Primary Stain
steps.instruction: Cover the entire smear with Carbol-fuchsine solution and let it sit for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Wash Slide
steps.instruction: Gently wash the slides with tap water using a dropper to avoid exposing the smear to high pressure.

steps.title: Decolorize Smear
steps.instruction: Apply 4-6 drops of decolorizer (Acid Alcohol) to the smear, then wash again with tap water.

steps.title: Counterstain Smear
steps.instruction: Apply counterstain (Methylene Blue, Gold Biotechnology Catalog #M-680), leave for 5 minutes, and wash with clean water.

steps.title: Examine Under Microscope
steps.instruction: Examine the smear using a compound microscope (Olympus, CH20i) with 40x and 100x (immersion oil lens) objectives to identify parasites.

steps.title: Clean and Dry Slides
steps.instruction: Clean the back side of the slides with tissue paper and place them in a draining rack to air-dry for 5 minutes.
